title: Born in Guadalajara
text: Luis Ramiro Barragán Morfín is born on 9 March in Guadalajara, Jalisco, into a family of landowners. Childhood summers at the family ranch near Mazamitla leave a lasting memory of adobe walls, water channels and village colour.

title: Engineering degree
text: Graduates as a civil engineer from the Escuela Libre de Ingenieros in Guadalajara. He never takes a formal degree in architecture.

title: First journey to Europe
text: Travels through France and Spain. The gardens of Ferdinand Bac and the Alhambra in Granada shape his understanding of the garden as an enclosed, private world.

title: Second journey
text: Visits New York and Paris, attends lectures by Le Corbusier and meets Ferdinand Bac in person.

title: Moves to Mexico City
text: Settles in the capital and works for several years as a developer and architect of functionalist apartment buildings.

title: Jardines del Pedregal
text: Plans the residential subdivision on the lava fields south of the city, with gardens and show houses that establish his mature language of walls, water and landscape.

title: Casa Barragán
text: Completes his own house and studio in Tacubaya, which he will continue to alter for the rest of his life.

title: Capuchinas chapel
text: Completes the chapel and convent for the Capuchinas Sacramentarias in Tlalpan, a study in coloured light.

title: Torres de Satélite
text: With Mathias Goeritz, builds the five coloured towers at the entrance to Ciudad Satélite.

title: Cuadra San Cristóbal
text: Completes the house, stables and pools for the Egerström family at Los Clubes, with Andrés Casillas.

title: Casa Gilardi
text: Completes the house in San Miguel Chapultepec, with its yellow corridor and indoor pool.

title: Casa Meyer
text: On 31 October he signs the elevation drawings for a house in Bosques de las Lomas for his friend Barbara Meyer, inscribed "para Baby Meyer de Garate, con todo cariño". It is his last residential project.

title: Pritzker Architecture Prize
text: Receives the Pritzker Prize. In his acceptance speech he speaks of serenity, silence, solitude and the garden.

title: Death in Mexico City
text: Dies on 22 November at his house in Tacubaya.

title: World Heritage
text: Casa Luis Barragán is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
